abstract: Loss-of-function (LOF) variants of the FLG gene are risk factors for atopic dermatitis. However, owing to the repetitive nature of exon 3, these variants are difficult to characterize. We sought to determine whether the use of long-read technologies would enable better characterization of the FLG gene and improve the detection of LOF variants. We sequenced a diverse clinical cohort of 192 samples collected in Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda using long-read sequencing as well as publicly available data. We identified both common and rare LOF variants linked to atopic dermatitis in our clinical cohort, a number of compound heterozygotes, as well as 1 previously undescribed LOF variant. We also observed 20 previously undescribed FLG alleles, which varied in length by up to 13 kb. These were mostly found in samples of sub-Saharan origin and appear to be products of nonallelic homologous recombination. Despite the use of a long-read-based approach, we did not detect any FLG LOF variants in our African cohort, highlighting differences in FLG LOF burden and atopic dermatitis genetic risk between populations. Our approach has the potential to be a useful tool to identify FLG variants contributing to atopic dermatitis in various human populations.
